habit_scope: Batt in exterior stud bays + interior vapor film on the warm side, after MEP rough, before drywall. AF&PA Insulation and Vapor Retarders is the US book. CMHC Ch5 6-mil poly combined air/vapour barrier is CANADIAN — label, do not copy R-values as Utah/Fontana habit. Title 24 is a Fontana MarketNote/hold, not a Utah batt copy. We do not have Title 24 text on disk.
how_it_is_done: After MEP rough inspection (CMHC Ch2: Insulation, Air Barrier System and Vapour Barrier after Plumbing/Heating/Electrical Rough-In). May run at the same time as exterior finishes if the insulated assembly is protected from wind-driven rain. A few days. Careful fitting and sealing around mechanical penetrations, fixtures and electrical boxes. Contact building official to inspect completed insulation, vapour barrier and air barrier. No skip-inspection.

AF&PA (US): roll or batt full thickness in exterior walls or between rafters. Roll or loose fill in attics between ceiling joists. Rigid foam plastic bonded to the inside of foundation walls with construction adhesive.

AF&PA vapor: kraft paper on batts is of little value because of gaps along each stud. Proper vapor protection = 4-mil (.004 in) minimum polyethylene film stapled to wall studs immediately beneath the drywall, carefully fitted around window and door openings and behind electric outlets. Crawl/slab moisture is 6-mil poly on the ground / under the slab (already P05). If foam or foil-faced sheathing is a vapor retarder on the outside, still put poly on the inside under the finish.

CMHC Ch5 (CANADIAN — confirm AHJ, do not copy as Utah/Fontana habit): combined air and vapour barrier often 0.15 mm (6 mil) polyethylene under gypsum, sealed at joints/penetrations, on the WARM side of the insulation. Air barrier is more important than vapour barrier for moisture movement. Housewrap on the exterior must be vapour-permeable if it is the air barrier outside the insulation. Fig 14: staple poly to studs and plate, lap seams ≥100 mm (4 in), acoustical sealant at perimeter and over seams in line with stud and plate. NBC minimum insulating values by heating-degree days — do not copy those R-values as Utah or Fontana habit.
CMHC batt: glass/mineral/slag; friction-fit slightly wider than the bay. Do not invent a Utah R-value from NBC tables.
Title 24: Fontana P13 hold point only. We do not have Title 24 text on disk. Do not invent the checklist. Do not copy a Utah batt as Title 24 compliance. See mn-fontana and gap-P13-title24-text.
HUD RSDG OPENED: not an insulation SOP. Essential Guide OPENED: framing, thin on insulation.

when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit. Foam sheathing / exterior insulation is a detailing add, not a new phase.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Copying NBC R-values onto Utah or Fontana. Treating kraft-faced batts as the vapor barrier (AF&PA). Skipping the insulation inspection. Inventing a Title 24 checklist.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They stuff batts. What they skip is poly under the drywall (AF&PA: kraft is not enough) and the inspection before hang.

risk_if_swapped_late: Changing wall R or vapor strategy after drywall is a tear-off. Catch before hang.
plain_language_summary: After rough-in, batts in the walls and a plastic sheet on the warm side under the drywall. AF&PA says 4-mil; the kraft on the batt is not enough. CMHC 6-mil poly is Canadian — ask the city before you copy it. Fontana Title 24 is a hold, not a Utah batt list. Inspector before hang.
